992cb085c9e477eb.summary: The evals workflow runs on a plain `pull_request` trigger (not `pull_request_target`) scoped only by a `paths` filter on CLAUDE.md/.claude/**/evals/**, so a pull request from any fork that touches one of those paths executes that fork's own copy of this workflow file and of sdlc.yaml's commands.setup, with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN available in the job's environment - letting an attacker who opens such a PR add a step (or a setup command) that exfiltrates both secrets over the open internet, since GitHub Actions runners are not subject to the project's own Claude-sandbox network allowlist.

d6f98f0dff40c7c4.reason: Dismissed: the guardrail policy is enforced by layers this review could not see, because it read only the project's settings. The pinned sdlc plugin's `shell_guard` hook denies a Bash or PowerShell command that names a guardrail file beside a write idiom: `git checkout <ref> -- CLAUDE.md`, `git restore`, `git rm`, `git mv`, `git apply`, and redirections such as `git show <ref>:sdlc.yaml > sdlc.yaml`. A git verb without a pathspec can change the working tree, but in CI the sandbox's `denyWrite` covers the guardrail files, the runner parks a phase whose branch changed one, the gate's guardrails check refuses the diff, and only the owner can merge to main. The CI sandbox proof is tracked upstream as sdlc-framework roadmap R44. `Bash(git *)` stays: sessions need it to commit and push. Report it again only if a guardrail change can reach main without the owner's merge.
d6f98f0dff40c7c4.summary: The permissions.deny list only blocks the Edit tool from touching guardrail files (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml), but permissions.allow grants unrestricted `Bash(git *)`, so any Claude session (build, test, fix, review) can overwrite those same files via git (e.g. `git checkout <ref> -- CLAUDE.md`, `git show <ref>:sdlc.yaml > sdlc.yaml`, or a direct commit+push) without ever invoking the denied Edit tool, defeating the 'owner changes guardrails only in a reviewed PR' policy stated in CLAUDE.md.

eda9f21137cf4079.reason: Dismissed: a deliberate setting, not a defect. `failIfUnavailable: false` in the project's `.claude/settings.json` is the framework template's documented choice (sdlc-framework NOTES §5): Claude Code's sandbox does not run on native Windows, where the owner works, and `true` would stop Claude Code from starting there. Every CI phase run passes the pinned framework's `plugin/ci/settings.ci.json` with `--settings`, which outranks this file and sets `failIfUnavailable: true` and `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, and the job installs bubblewrap first. It is not SSRF. Report it again only if the CI settings stop requiring the sandbox.
eda9f21137cf4079.summary: sandbox.failIfUnavailable is false, so on any runner where the OS-level sandbox cannot be initialized the session silently runs unsandboxed instead of stopping, dropping the sandbox's network allow-list (github.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org) that is supposed to bound every outbound call a session's allowed Bash commands (e.g. `git push`, `pip install`) can make.
